prompt: Compute $8{,}649 \div 31$ using long division. Give your answer as a **decimal**.
hint: Long division works one digit at a time from the left. After each subtraction the remainder must be **less than** $31$ before you bring down the next digit.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm-up: try $93 \div 31$ first. $31 \times 3 = 93$, so $93 \div 31 = 3$. Carry that intuition forward.
Long division works one digit at a time from the left. After each subtraction the remainder must be **less than** $31$ before you bring down the next digit.
Start with $86$: $31$ goes in $2$ times, leaving $24$. Bring down the $4$ to make $244$, find how many times $31$ fits, subtract, then bring down the $9$ and repeat once more.
The quotient digits are $2$, $7$ and $9$ with no remainder, so $8{,}649 \div 31 = 279$.

explanation: Estimate first so you can check the result: $8649 \div 30$ is close to $288$, so expect a three-digit answer near $280$.
Divide $31$ into $86$. Since $31 \times 2 = 62$ fits and $31 \times 3 = 93$ is too big, the first digit is $2$. Subtract to get $86 - 62 = 24$ and bring down the $4$ to make $244$.
Divide $31$ into $244$. Since $31 \times 7 = 217$ fits and $31 \times 8 = 248$ is too big, the next digit is $7$. Subtract to get $27$ and bring down the $9$ to make $279$.
Divide $31$ into $279$. Here $31 \times 9 = 279$ exactly, so the last digit is $9$ and the remainder is $0$.
Reading the digits in order gives $8649 \div 31 = 279$, which matches the estimate.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check by multiplying back
steps: If multiplying back doesn't hit the original dividend, redo the long division.

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate to spot mistakes
steps: So the true answer should be **close to but a little less than** $300$. $279$ fits.
If you had gotten $2790$ or $28$, the estimate would have flagged the missing place value.
